# Policy-as-Code for AI | Your 2026 Operating Model. Enterprises won’t be graded in 2026 on the flashiness of their demos, they’ll be judged on how safely, explainably, and cost-consciously they run AI in production. In BFSI, Government, Education, Healthcare and Telecom, the differentiator is an operating model that makes models first-class artifacts: versioned, signed, gated by policy, budget-bounded on GPUs, and observable for audit on demand. If your AI pipeline still lives outside CI/CD and evidence is a quarter-end scramble, you don’t have a strategy; you have exposure. Models, adapters, prompts, datasets and plugins all need provenance, signatures and attestations enforced in the pipeline, not in a PDF. Controls must block non-conforming releases and emit export-ready evidence continuously. * Model SBOM + signatures: SBOMs for base models, adapters, datasets; release gates reject unsigned artifacts. * Policy-as-Code in the path to prod: Admission controllers enforce residency, PII/PHI constraints, bias and red-team thresholds. * Budget-gated GPUs: Per-team ceilings; preemptive rules for burst vs baseline work; idle shutdowns by default. * Runtime evidence: Trace prompts, guardrail triggers and mitigations; alerts are mapped to control IDs for audit. * BFSI: KYC/loan decisions require lineage and explainability; AI changes are gated like code. * Public sector: Residency and sovereign controls are non-negotiable; every response leaves a reviewable footprint. * Education: Semester peaks demand elastic capacity; off-season costs collapse with policy-driven shutdown. It matures when governance is compiled into the pipeline and cost is treated as a reliability signal. Treat models like software artifacts, wire controls as code, and make evidence as routine as logs. Taashee brings the connective tissue: content governance, DevSecOps→ModelOps tooling, GPU guardrails, and day-2 compliance that works at runtime, not just on slides. ###### Share this post. ### Related Posts. ## Policy-as-Code for AI | Your 2026 Operating Model. results.title: Simple checklist for ML reproducibility
results.content: # Simple checklist for ML reproducibility | by Jaideep Ray | Better ML | Medium. ## Better ML. # Simple checklist for ML reproducibility. Reproducing a study is a common practice for most developers/researchers as this can help confirm findings, get inspiration from others’ work, and avoid reinventing the wheel. In this our scope is to discuss reproducibility aspects of ml models (or more generally a trained ML systems). > **Reproducibility** refers to the ability of a researcher to duplicate the results of a prior study using the same materials as were used by the original investigator [1]. *   **Privacy and policy audits** : Privacy and policy audits are only possible if all aspects of ml system (code, data and model) are understood and accessible for duplicating it. ML systems deal with code, large amounts of data and models (probabilistic in nature). *   We describe a set of best practices and tooling for ml system reproducibility. This contains artifacts and metadata for code, data and model reproducibility.

results.content: # Code World Model. Code World Model (CWM) is a 32-billion-parameter open-weights LLM, to advance research on code generation with world models. The CWM release includes model weights (pre-trained, SFT and instruction-tuned), the technical report, the model card and starting code to run inference with the model, and reproduce the reported numbers on key benchmarks such as SWE-bench Verified, LiveCodeBench, AIME and MATH. We introduce Code World Model (CWM). CWM is an LLM for code generation and reasoning about code that has, in particular, been trained to better represent and reason about how code and commands affect the state of a program or system. The model weights are available on Hugging Face for use with vLLM. Please refer to the model card below for model details, more information on uses, risks and limitations as well as the license under which the weights are released. For example and starting code to use CWM from the Hugging Face weights, please refer to the model card.

results.title: Openness in Language Models: Open Source vs Open Weights vs Restricted Weights
results.content: # Openness in Language Models: Open Source vs Open Weights vs Restricted Weights. As language models hype "openness", this article proposes key criteria to evaluate true transparency balanced with safety. By clearly delineating the differences between open weights versus full open source access, I establish a framework for evaluating claims of openness. Releasing weights allows models to be used but limits inspectability and community control. In the context of AI, open source refers to the availability of the source code for modification and distribution. In the context of AI, open weights refer to the availability of these weights for use or modification. ## Open Weights vs Open Source for Language Models. **So, open weights allows model use but not full transparency, while open source enables model understanding and customization but requires substantially more work to release.** The choice between these two approaches involves important tradeoffs for both model creators and consumers.
